get_active_lifecycle_summary.description: One summary row per open PR on the repo (pr_number, title, stage, action, head_sha, url). For 'what's in flight right now?' dashboards / orchestrator polls.

get_pr_lifecycle_state.description: Lifecycle stage + per-stage timestamps + next-action hint for one PR. Single call replaces seven primitives (PR labels, check-runs, ai-review comments, Tide eligibility, jx-promote PR state, GitOps reconcile).

owner.description: GitHub owner; defaults to mikelear when empty

get_pr_lifecycle_timeline.description: Chronological list of observed transitions for a PR. Reconstructed from observable timestamps — no stored-history requirement.

owner.description: GitHub owner; defaults to mikelear when empty

get_release_state.description: Where is image:version in its release journey (registry mirrors, signing, scanning, promote, reconcile)? Best-effort: registry probe failures collapse to false rather than raising.

list_pr_checks.description: Snapshot of every check-run on a PR — one row per <cluster>/<check> with state (success|failure|pending|neutral), PipelineRun name + SHA + timestamps. Retires the gh-pr-checks shim; sources direct from Tekton PipelineRun state so cross-cluster asymmetry (green on gcp, red on az) is visible at a glance.

run_id.description: calling AgentRun name, for Loki correlation

post_pr_handoff.description: Upsert this run's sticky handoff comment on the PR — the durable note a successor iteration reads FIRST. Call it freely (every loop is fine): the comment is rewritten only when the state actually changes, so frequent calls are cheap and an iteration killed mid-flight still leaves its last known state behind. Scoped per run_id, and explicitly labelled a hint rather than truth, because authoritative state is the PR's checks plus Keeper's merge status.

budget_state.description: ok | approaching_limit | exhausted; derived from turns when omitted

evidence.description: short factual lines a successor should not have to rediscover

iteration.description: this run's iteration number, if known

model.description: the model actually served, which may differ from the one requested

next_step.description: the single next action a successor should take

run_id.description: calling AgentRun name; scopes the sticky comment and joins Loki

summary.description: what is true right now, for the next iteration to read first

turns_max.description: the max_turns ceiling this run was given

turns_used.description: turns consumed so far; only the agent knows this

verdict.description: the current verdict, e.g. a pr_gate_snapshot verdict

pr_gate_snapshot.description: One call: is this PR mergeable, and what should I do next? Reads GitHub commit statuses (cluster-attributed and what Keeper actually gates on, so both estates are covered, unlike the Tekton-backed tools) plus the PR's labels, and returns a verdict: WAIT (checks running, or green+approved so Keeper will merge), FIX (a check failed — read its target_url log FIRST, because a red context can be a publish/infrastructure failure whose work passed and needs /retest not a code change), STOP (blocked_needs_human, e.g. green but no `approved` label), DONE (merged). Never reports success from an empty check list.

run_id.description: calling AgentRun name, for Loki correlation

wait_for_first_failure_or_all_pass.description: Fail-fast wait: return as soon as ANY check fails OR all checks pass. Returns {status: first_failure|all_passed|timeout, first_failure, checks}. Surface a lint failure in ~15s while end2end is still running so the agent iterates on a fresh commit instead of waiting for the slowest check.

run_id.description: calling AgentRun name, for Loki correlation

wait_for_terminal.description: Block until every check on the PR reaches a terminal state (success|failure) or timeout_seconds elapses. Returns {status: all_passed|some_failed|timeout, checks}. Use before the final 'ready for review' sticky — want every check settled.

run_id.description: calling AgentRun name, for Loki correlation

get_pr_diff.description: Unified diff for a PR. Without pattern returns the full diff. With pattern (suffix like '.spec.ts') returns only the matching changed file paths.

get_pr_metadata.description: Canonical PR context: head/base SHA, head branch (head_ref), title, body, state, merged flag + merged_at timestamp, changed files, labels + mergeable_state + a computed `held` boolean. Two GitHub REST calls (PR object + files list). Use `merged` to disambiguate MERGED vs CLOSED-unmerged — GitHub reports both as state=closed. Use `held` (or the `labels` list) to verify a `do-not-merge/*` label is present before treating the PR as safely blocked from auto-merge.

repo.description: the repo name (bare like 'webcoder-ui' or owner/name form)

list_changed_files.description: Just the list of changed file paths (no diff body, no metadata).

open_pr.description: Ensure a PR exists on the branch and authoritatively record it — IDEMPOTENT (adopt-or-create). Creates via POST /pulls, or if an open PR already exists on the head branch ADOPTS it (a resumed/re-spawned dev agent, or a Dev agent taking over an Infra-opened PR) — never a duplicate-create error. The PR number + head branch come from STRUCTURED API JSON (never scraped), then it patches the calling AgentRun's status.targetPR + status.headBranch (controller emits Maestro run.pr_opened). PUSH your branch first, then call this INSTEAD of `gh pr create` — safe to call on resume. Inputs: run_id (LEARTECH_RUN_ID), namespace, repo (owner/repo), base, head, title, body. Optional test_mode=true (or leartech.io/test-mode annotation on the AgentRun) requests the SYNTHETIC path: no GitHub call, a fake PR number in the 999xxxxx range, same AgentRun.status patch — honored only when the cluster env LEARTECH_MCP_TEST_MODE_ALLOWED is truthy (a stray test_mode on a production pod is silently demoted to the real GitHub path).

resolve_pr.description: READ the PR this run produced — the query counterpart to open_pr's command. Resolves AUTHORITATIVE-first: AgentRun.status.targetPR (the value open_pr wrote — state-agnostic, SURVIVES a merge), then a GitHub fallback for the branch's PR in ANY state ("all", not "open") so a MERGED PR (a success) is visible. Strictly READ-ONLY: no PR create, no status patch — use this (never open_pr) to CHECK whether a run produced a PR. Inputs: run_id (LEARTECH_RUN_ID, optional — omit to resolve purely by branch), namespace (required to read status.targetPR), repo (owner/repo or bare), head (the pushed branch). Returns {found, number, state, merged, head_ref, url, source} where source is status|github|none.

head.description: the head branch the agent pushed

namespace.description: the AgentRun namespace; required to read status.targetPR

run_id.description: the AgentRun name (LEARTECH_RUN_ID) whose status.targetPR is authoritative; optional

cancel_pipelinerun.description: Cancel one PipelineRun via a merge-patch that sets spec.status=PipelineRunCancelled. Use after a force-push supersedes an in-flight run. Returns {cancelled: bool}.

cancel_superseded_for_pr.description: Cancel every in-flight PipelineRun on this PR whose lastCommitSHA differs from keep_sha. Skips already-terminal runs. Returns {cancelled_count: N}.

keep_sha.description: the SHA whose PipelineRuns must NOT be cancelled

diagnose_pr_failures.description: One-shot cross-cluster failure diagnosis for a PR. Per failing check returns the failed step, exit code, log tail, classification + recommended action.

list_pipelineruns_for_pr.description: Discover Tekton PipelineRuns attached to a GitHub PR via Lighthouse refs.repo+refs.pull labels. Returns newest-first.

release_pipeline_status.description: Release-verification steps 1+2: did a release pipeline FIRE (a PipelineRun exists) and PASS for a commit? A release runs on a MAIN-PUSH postsubmit with NO PR number, so list_pipelineruns_for_pr can't find it — this keys on the commit SHA (lastCommitSHA label). Inputs: repo, sha (the merged/pushed main commit), cluster (az|gcp, default az). Returns {fired, passed, running, failed, run, runs, cluster}.

repo.description: the repo whose main-push release pipeline to check (bare or owner/name)

sha.description: the release-triggering commit SHA (the merged/pushed main commit); runs are matched by the lastCommitSHA label

step_logs.description: Tail of stdout+stderr from one step of one PipelineRun (default 200 lines). Empty string when pod is GC'd.

step_name.description: the step name within the PipelineRun

step_status.description: Walk a PipelineRun and return per-step verdicts {task, step, state, reason, exit_code, pod}.

wait_first_failure.description: Step-aware fail-fast wait: returns within one poll of any step failing on the PR (e.g. a ruff failure surfaces in ~15s even while pytest is still running). Returns {status: first_failure|all_passed|timeout, first_failure, runs}.
